title: Merdith et al. (2021) continuous full-plate motion model, 1 Ga to present
citation: Merdith, A. S., Williams, S. E., Collins, A. S., Tetley, M. G., Mulder, J. A., Blades, M. L., Young, A., Armistead, S. E., Cannon, J., Zahirovic, S., and Müller, R. D., 2021. Extending full-plate tectonic models into deep time: Linking the Neoproterozoic and the Phanerozoic. Earth-Science Reviews, 214, 103477.

license.note: Attribution and citation are required. Unlike the PALEOMAP maps this project also uses, publishing derived work on a website needs no further consent.

limitations: The authors state the model is in a purely palaeomagnetic reference frame and is unsuitable for Pacific hotspot kinematics or for analyses shorter than 5 Ma. Longitude in the Precambrian is weakly constrained by palaeomagnetism alone.
preferred_note: Shown first: the palaeomagnetic frame is the one the authors point to for climate-sensitive reading, and it is the fairer comparison against the published maps.
notes: Manifest pinned from EarthThruTime3D sources/plate-models/merdith2021.json at be59c3a, with the topology and static-polygon members added. The rotation file is byte-identical to Rotations/1000_0_rotfile.rot in the Müller et al. 2022 v1.2.4 Zenodo record (sha256 9ab561d7…, checked 2026-11-12), so the same palaeomagnetic frame is also available under CC BY 4.0 there.
